properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/24/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/24/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 989692
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple produced fluid releases on Pad B as well as sediment discharges from the access road. The site is no longer snow-covered. No new sediment discharges were observed along the access road. The temporary E and S BMPs at stream crossings and wetlands along the access road appear to be functioning as designed. On Pad B, the GPUs and production tanks have been installed within secondary containment. The flow lines and production lines have been installed and the trenches have been backfilled. Batteries of frac tanks were being set up within secondary containment during this inspection. The secondary containment for the evaporators was being installed as well. The sump and north stormwater channel have not yet been remediated. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 981 uS/cm. The EC of the fluid in the north stormwater channel was 2500 uS/cm toward the east end and 1680 uS/cm farther to the west.The outstanding violations against the ESCGP for sediment discharges along the access road into streams and wetlands will be closed. Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation ID: 8198343
Permit API: 065-26670
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3765073), I noted API 065-26670 did not have a well tag, and there was evidence of a production fluid release. The spill appeared to be greater than 5 gallons but less than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790399), I noted the operator installed a new tag and seeded and mulched the spill area. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the visual cleanup of the site. The tag violation was closed. As of today the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts and waste manifests regarding the visual clean up of this site. As I was leaving the Wheeler sites, I ran into Ray Hepler. He stated that the contaminated soil from the visual clean-up was added to the same truck containing soil from the southwest, and that he would eventually be providing tipping an manifest information. The outstanding violations will remain open until the Department receives tipping receipts and waste manifests.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/16/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/16/2022
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 948136
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: On March 16, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline and Brooke Millisock conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The DEP observed and sampled five seeps and four stream sites that were found off the west side of the well pad in "Deep Hollow" along an UNT to Rattlesnake Run. STL Resources revealed that the seeps were occurring and being monitored for specific conductivity and chlorides on March 1, 2022 during a meeting with the DEP. The data that STL Resources provided showed levels of elevated conductivity in seeps 1, 1A, and 4. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling site for pH and conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 had a pH of 8.61 and conductivity of 29.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/23/2021
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 921782
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/23/2021
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both pads. DEP Environmental Trainee John Rogers and DEP Geoscientist Sam Louderback accompanied me on this inspection. We met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on Pad B. On Pad B, the sump remains installed where fluid with elevated conductivity (EC) was observed on the pad surface. Fluid is present within the sump approximately two feet below the pad surface. The EC of this fluid is 2.19 mS/cm. No elevated conductivity fluid was observed on or off the pad. In the rock-lined ditch along the northwest edge of the pad, two small puddles of fluid were found which had a petroleum odor and a sheen. I notified the company man of the presence of these puddles before leaving the location. On Pad A, we met with company man Grant Boyd upon arriving on location. He told us that excavation had been done after the previous inspection on the pad near the northeast corner of the well site secondary containment. Multiple puddles were observed in this area during this inspection which had an EC between 3.43 mS/cm and 4.33 mS/cm. An additional puddle was observed along the pad edge within the brush barrier along the side of the pad. This puddle had an EC of 2.09 mS/cm. I took a sample, sample #0718-178, from this puddle and sent it to the state laboratory the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Li, Br, and Al. I notified the company man of my findings before leaving the location. In a phone call with Rick Hall on the same day at 13:29, I relayed my observations on both pads to Mr. Hall. He said that he would have the puddles investigated and remediated. Violations remain outstanding for the release on Pad B.

Comments: On 11/08/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well. The following was observed:Operator and well information on site (Photos 1, 2). I recommend placing the rest of the well information on the same sign that has the operator information.Pumpjack in motion upon arrival, some grease/oil on gravel. I recommend removal (Photo 3). Wellhead, production equipment were in generally good condition (Photos 2-5). Mild corrosion. Additional equipment adjacent to the well approximately 40 feet away - there is a depression around the equipment and it is filled with water; dead vegetation around depression, no high conductivity reading. I recommend addressing the depression and exploring the cause of the depression and dead vegetation - unclear if cause if from equipment or pooled water (Photos 6).Downslope of the well were five production tanks within an earthen berm. The berm was in generally good condition, however the pooled water within the berm contained high conductivity readings, specifically in front of tank 1. The sediment within the berm had adequate readings, however the rest of the pooled water had slightly elevated readings. A slightly elevated conductivity reading was taken within the gravel/sediment below the valve of tank 5. This area was relatively small and is recommended that any affected material is removed and disposed of properly. A corroded piece of equipment noted near tank 5 (Photos 7-22, see captions for specific locations). I notified the operator while onsite; a vac truck later was there removing the fluid as I was leaving. Plans are to add equipment to catch fluids when the vac truck removes the hose from the valves. It is noted that the access road has multiple uses, including agricultural, however the access roads to the well sites require routine monitoring and maintenance.Due to the observation of elevated conductivity readings within the pooled water and prompt remediation, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being noted and were immediately corrected. A follow up inspection to ensure there is not residual production fluids within the berm. No additional violations are being issued right now, however additional violations may be forthcoming.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-05-29 to Bkv Opr Llc in Washington Twp, Wyoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Bkv Opr Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-05-29
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 851857
Permit API: 131-20585
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-05-29
Comments: I arrived at the site at 10:34 in response to a reported spill incident of an unknown volume of a fluid substance spilled to the pad surface, and into stormwater in a site perimeter ditch. The weather conditions are partly cloudy skies, breezy, warm and humid, with temperatures in the low to mid 70's. Representing the Department during the inspection in addition to myself include Ken Kennedy, Eric Miller, Cassidy Moyer and Eric Rooney. Marvin Schellie, consultant of BKV, is the company man at the site. Representing BKV is Tom Weller, Matt Knight and Dale Bennett. Representing the BKV consultant Apex Environmental is Shelly Bowen, and Jamie Moran. Kevin Brady of Whitetail Environmental, a BKV consultant, is also at the site. The current drilling depth on the Reynolds 2H well is (3,096) feet. Air drilling is in progress. The intermediate casing was cemented on 5/27/19 according to Mr. Schellie. Mr. Weller explained that inadvertently, a bypass valve for an overflow line was left open on the Iron Horse shale gas separator. Following waiting on cement (WOC), displacement fluid was being unloaded from the intermediate casing, and the existing separator tank was half full. When changed over and pressuring up to resume air drilling, air and some remaining displacement fluid was inadvertently discharged across the open top tank under pressure, and overflowed the tank and containment. Mr. Weller estimated that less than (1) barrel (42) gallons, was released off containment. Mr. Weller explained that the displaced water was recycled from previous air drilling operations, which may include the use of various lube products, and air foaming and defoaming products. Mr. Brady provided the Department with Safety Data Sheets (SDS) of the products. The SDS indicates the chemical name for the lube product is ECO Drill 100, with biodegradable drill oil listed as a synonym. The SDS indicates the foaming product is FoamFresh, with Eco-Friendly Foamer listed as a synonym. Mr. Brady also provided the Department with photos of the source of the fluid spilled out of the container, the ditch which is labeled stormwater channel, and a map of the site. The container is located on secondary containment in the area on the pad surface termed the backyard by BKV. This particular area is located adjacent to the drilling rig and site perimeter berm. Mr. Brady informed the Department that he recorded specific conductance (conductivity) of (4) millisiemens/cm in water in the stormwater channel on 5/28/19 at 15:35, (145) parts per million in chlorides on a Hach test strip on 5/28/19 at 15:35, and a sump was constructed in the channel as a result of the elevated readings. He further stated that an on-site vacuum truck was immediately deployed to the area where the spill occurred, and an additional vacuum truck was dispatched to remove impacted stormwater in the channel. Apex informed the Department they screened the impacted area on the ground surface with a photoionization detector (PID) meter for the potential presence of volatile organic compounds at 8:24 AM today, 5/29/19, and screened the water in the channel for conductivity at 8:40 AM today, 5/29/19. Apex indicated they excavated small holes in (3) locations on the berm where the impact occurred, to obtain PID readings. The reading at the first location was (1.9) ppm; the second location was (1.6) ppm, and the third location was 1.5 ppm. The PID meter read (0) parts per million on containment near the tank as part of the release. Conductivity was (306) microsiemens/cm. I used a Hanna HI 98331 Groline Soil Test meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record conductivity of water in the channel. During the inspection, the Department and Apex collected samples of stormwater in the channel in (3) separate locations. The Department also collected a sample of fluid in the container associated with the spill. See photos. The Department left the site at 13:28.

Report Details

Violation ID: 964168
Permit API: 085-24071
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Delaware Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/08/2022
Comments: Received phone call from Matt Kleese (Diamond Energy) earlier this morning informing me of incident and providing me an update of operation status. Additionally, correspondence records and documents received by OGI, Thomas Antonishak from the Department pertaining to the incident and emergency response occurring over the weekend. Arrived at location on 8/8/2022 to met with Operator representatives (Diamond Energy), Rick Wiley, OGI Supervisor, and property land owner on site late morning with warm, slightly windy, cloudy weather conditions, and 76 degrees. The well is being vented back to the 100 bbl steel tank at the ground production facility with the tank vent open to atmosphere. Change out rabbit catcher and attempt to pump into well. The well continues to build pressure, requiring additional time to bleed pressure as necessary to control. Unable to pump into well at this time (photos #1 and #2). Routine and complete inspection in response to incident of well catching fire after a lightning strike that was witnessed by the property land owner during a thunderstorm on August 5, 2022 at approximately 2042 hours. The address for the property is 18 Wasser Road, Greenville, PA 16125. The well is located in Delaware Township, Mercer County, PA. The well is operated, since 2020 by Diamond Energy Partners with issued permit number 085-24071 on 4/13/2006, spud date was on 8/31/2007, drilled to total depth of 5,290 feet, Site ID# 669360, and is a conventional vertical gas well. Wellhead is located in livestock pasture/field and ~550' WNW of surface/ground production equipment. At the wellhead, all tubulars, valves, domestic meter, and unions are all damaged by the fire. The ground surface, and area approximately 10 ft x 20 ft around the well in this area is burnt with stressed vegetation. The fire appeared contained to in and around the wellhead area, which was enclosed by a metal cattle guard. No oil residue present on ground (photos #2, #3, #4, and #5). Unable to determine if well label/marker was present due to the fire damage. The surface/ground production equipment, one 100 bbl steel, and one 50 bbl poly tank(s) are contained by earthen dike (photos #6 and #7). Inadequate well posting signage present on 100 bbl steel tank. Only posting Operator name and phone number. No other well details present - needs updated and replaced (photo #7). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and steel tanks. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The mechanical integrity assessment (MIA) report and submitted by Operator (Diamond) for 2021 for this well states 800 psig. The last reported, commercial production was in 2016 of 1,081 MCF recorded over 84 days by former Operator, Bobcat Well and Pipeline. The 2021 annual production report (APR) submitted by present Operator (Diamond) indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021 production report. There is mention of domestic house gas under additional comments column on 2017 and 2018 APRs, but not mentioned in prior or post years. In talking with the property land owner, domestic house gas has been provided uninterruptedly to residence since the initial drilling of the well back in 2007. Conversation with the Operator (Diamond) also concurs domestic house gas supply to landowner. Albeit no commercial production to sales reported by Operator, stating 0 production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns, the well is active and providing domestic house gas continuously and will be restored once repairs to wellhead are completed. The Department is requesting the Operator (Diamond) provide a copy of the Preparedness Prevention and Contingency Plan (PPC) document for this well and well site facility.

Wellhead is located in livestock pasture/field and ~550' WNW of surface/ground production equipment. At the wellhead, all tubulars, valves, domestic meter, and unions are all damaged by the fire. The ground surface, and area approximately 10 ft x 20 ft around the well in this area is burnt with stressed vegetation. The fire appeared contained to in and around the wellhead area, which was enclosed by a metal cattle guard. No oil residue present on ground (photos #2, #3, #4, and #5). Unable to determine if well label/marker was present due to the fire damage. The surface/ground production equipment, one 100 bbl steel, and one 50 bbl poly tank(s) are contained by earthen dike (photos #6 and #7). Inadequate well posting signage present on 100 bbl steel tank. Only posting Operator name and phone number. No other well details present - needs updated and replaced (photo #7). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and steel tanks. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The mechanical integrity assessment (MIA) report and submitted by Operator (Diamond) for 2021 for this well states 800 psig. The last reported, commercial production was in 2016 of 1,081 MCF recorded over 84 days by former Operator, Bobcat Well and Pipeline. The 2021 annual production report (APR) submitted by present Operator (Diamond) indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021 production report. There is mention of domestic house gas under additional comments column on 2017 and 2018 APRs, but not mentioned in prior or post years. In talking with the property land owner, domestic house gas has been provided uninterruptedly to residence since the initial drilling of the well back in 2007. Conversation with the Operator (Diamond) also concurs domestic house gas supply to landowner. Albeit no commercial production to sales reported by Operator, stating 0 production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns, the well is active and providing domestic house gas continuously and will be restored once repairs to wellhead are completed. The Department is requesting the Operator (Diamond) provide a copy of the Preparedness Prevention and Contingency Plan (PPC) document for this well and well site facility.

Comments: This well was in production at the time of inspection. There were several pieces of farming equipment staged on the edges of the pad and there was garbage piles located on the far side of the pad. The well head was properly equipped with a well ID tag and the site posting was intact at the entrance to the well road. The AST had several holes located in the sides and top. The well also appeared to be discharging gas into the AST at the time of inspection. Merchbaker reached out to OWS to gather information about this and has yet to hear back.The secondary containment of the AST was holding approximately 2ft of water at the time of inspection. This water tested normally with a conductivity probe and appeared to be stormwater. The secondary containment also had what appeared to be a low spot in the containment wall where the water was very close to releasing from. Merchbaker spoke with the landowner and he stated that the farm equipment was his and that he would move it if necessary. He stated that OWS had not mentioned it needing to be moved and also stated that he encountered a person claiming to be affiliated with OWS at 6am one morning attempting to drain the secondary containment with a sump pump. After speaking to the landowner this individual left in a hurry according to the landowner. Merchbaker will be following up on this site.

Comments: On April 14, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The hole in the well pad trench liner near the northwest stormwater vault has been fixed. Two patches have been added to the trench liner. The soil in the area where the water from the seep had been pooling up has been excavated and removed. A small berm has been built in the area and a tarp has been dug in to collect stormwater. This area is being vacuumed as necessary. The DEP screened the pooled water on the downgradient side of the built berm and the conductivity was 365 uS/cm. An area to the south of the area impacted from the seep of the northwest stormwater vault that had been previously excavated to remove contaminated soil from the seep was screened for soil conductivity. The screening resulted in a measurement of 2.42 mS/cm in a small area. The area of high conductivity was shown to STL Resources Ken Shade. There was about 8 inches of water in northwest stormwater vault. About 12 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in either vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There has been no pad surface remediation completed. The DEP screened the five seeps and three stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.4. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 190 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 274 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32.6 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 40.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 169.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. Infiltration berm 1 along the access road that had a section erode observed on February 18, 2022 has been filled in and compost filter sock has been added near the berm. The other four infiltration berms with erosion noted in Inspection Report 3324293 have been filled in. The infiltration berms along the access road have not been seeded or temporarily stabilized. It appears that earth work on the infiltration berms along the access road has been completed. The DEP recommend seeding and temporarily stabilizing the infiltration berms according to ¿102.22(b). This will help with preventing another situation of sediment discharging outside of the LOD and help prevent accelerated erosion of bare earth. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late morning with cold, cloudy weather conditions, and 30 degrees. Last inspection performed on 7/26/18, more than 4 years ago. Wellhead is located in Agriculture field planted and harvested with soybean ~250' WSW of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with closed valve to port and plumbed to drip/domestic house gas meter run, valve closed to stuffing box before meter and valve closed after meter to supply, production tubular left side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with closed valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #3 and #4). Meter reading and closed supply valve (photo #5). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker. Some trace to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #6). Valve closed on main tubular feeding facility and closed valves to and from separator (photo #7). No production chart recording apparatus present (photo #8). No Well posting signage is affixed anywhere at or near facility. Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment. Oil staining present at facility on ground near separator with in the containment (photos #6 and #7). Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add permanent well posting signage to be affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, and 2017 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2015 of 25.55 Mcf recorded over 336 days. This well continues to not be in production with valves closed (shut-in) at the wellhead to sales/production and to plumbed meter run before and after meter. Additionally, the main valve to facility is closed and there is not production recording chart apparatus at facility. This well has not reported production in over five years. This is not an active, producing well. The well is abandoned. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well abandonment OGA3220(A).

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

Comments: On March 7, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3482092 where it was found that although contaminated soil was removed from the point of impact, contamination from the stockpile was found to be leaching into the soil downslope. Recurring violations were issued as a result. The operator then explained that the tarp which was used to cover it must have been removed by inclement weather, and then proceeded to cover it with reinforced tarp and surround it with straw and silt fence. Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/31/2025
Comments: On January 31, 2025 the Department conducted an Incident inspection of the PF Eisaman South 43 well pad located in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on Monday, January 27, 2025. Accompanying on today's inspection is CNX representative Jessie Valentine. Mr. Valentine showed the Department the area where the spill occurred and stated that the spill occurred due to a piping/equipment failure, and that the release was approximately two barrels of production fluid.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Valentine stated that remediation efforts had occurred, and that fresh gravel has been laid in the spill area. The Department observed a large area between the production tanks and GPUs where new gravel appeared to be laid. The Department took a background soil conductivity reading upslope on the well pad's perimeter (0.0894 mS), and then took several readings in the area where fresh gravel was laid (0.0103 mS, 0.492 mS, 0.0436 mS, 9.68 mS, 6.38 mS, 0.787 mS, and 0.413 mS) to assess if any impacted materials remained on site. These soil conductivity readings when compared to the background soil conductivity reading subjugate that there are still some areas where the spill has not been fully excavated. Mr. Valentine spray painted the areas where the Department took elevated readings at, so they can easily identified for future remediation. The Department recommends the Operator fully remediate the release and dispose of all contaminated material properly and in accordance with regulations. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, plan for further remediation of the spill or release and assessment of any impacts to water of the Commonwealth. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled and is requesting the Operator follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2). At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and inside the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) Plan. The Ac 9 sign had a different Operator than the ERP and PPC Plan, the Department recommends the Operator update all plans as applicable. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel and no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed, and all of the well pad perimeters appeared to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the well pad had 6 wells on it on it as well as 3 production tanks within secondary containment and 6 GPUs within secondary containment, at the time of this inspection no active fluid leaks or fluid discharge were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. The 2H well (SPUD 4/20/2017) had a well tag fixed to it with the API number on it, but this well tag did not have any of the Operator's information on it. The Department is recommending the Operator update the well tag and/or well posting to have all required information posted on it in accordance with 3211(g). While on site, the Department spoke with CNX representative Chad Eisenman via the phone to inform him of the Department's findings during this inspection and verbally requested the aforementioned information.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for an approximately 2 barrel release of production fluid onto the well pad. A subsequent inspection will be conducted to assess further remedial measures. An Act 2 Report has not yet been submitted to the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

Permit API: 117-21652
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/14/2024
Comments: On 3/14/2024, Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Watkins Unit 820 well site located in Chatham Twp, Tioga Co. This was in response to spill notification CID# 378902 of a release of produced water and oil-based mud to a 40'x40' section of the pad surface. The release was reported as coming from the annulus of a plugged well on site.It was 55 degrees and clear when I arrived on site. I met up with DEP inspectors, Lester Tayler and Scotty Brown. Prior to my arrival, Lester received the following information from Seneca's Rick Dake: Rick discovered the release on 3/14/2024 at 1500 hours. Fluid was on the pad surface and was spitting out and leaking from the 13x9 annulus of the Watkins 25H plugged OG well. Rick explained the release as being caused by rainwater flowing across the pad and into the 25H well cellar. The rainwater flowed down the annulus and pushed the lighter weight oil-based mud to surface. During the inspection, I did witness a crew using two excavators and a small front-end loader to scrape the area north and east of the 25H well cellar of loose gravel. The gravel they were scraping was wet and dark colored. The pad surface was void of water puddles and was a lighter color. This excavation area extended approximately 40' from the south side of the well cellar to the north with production equipment limiting the extent of the excavation. Dark staining marked the pad surface as the release spread on an eastward path to the riprap lined channel below the cut slope on the east side of the pad. I did witness dark brownish black blobs of liquid floating on water within the riprap channel. 3-inch boom absorbents had been placed within the riprap lined channel at the north and south extents of the visible contamination. The distance between the north and south booms was approximately 50 feet.Miller Environmental Group was on site providing cleanup activities to the site. Miller's project manager, Ernie Ginoble, said that he had responded to the site at 1500 on 3/13/2024 and provided initial response actions while assessing the scene. The cleanup crew mobilized equipment to the site on 3/14/2024 at 0630. He said that they were scraping down approximately 6 inches to a cemented layer of the pad. They were placing the excavated material into plastic-lined rolloff dumpsters that were being staged on secondary containment on the southwest corner of the pad. Prior to my leaving, they had filled three dumpsters with two more available at the site. A vac truck was on site sucking up free liquids from the pad surface and from the 25H well cellar. A vac box arrived at the site during the inspection to allow for additional volume.There is a house and a farm north of the property and houses south of the property. I did not witness any residential property to the east or to the west. The area is pasture type grasses. There is a stream across the road to the west.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c).During a phone conversation after the inspection, Seneca's Jeff Passerrello did report that Seneca will pursue Act 2 for the release.I departed the site at 1350 hours.

Comments: On 06/03/2026 at 0017 hours the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a notification of a release at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County (CTS #398207). Representative Ralph Babcock stated "on 6/2/26 at 5:15 p.m., a Keystone Clear Water truck driver was loading production water when the line split releasing 25 gallons of produced water. Approximately 10 gallons of produced water spilled into a containment structure while the remaining 15 gallons of produced water spilled onto the ground. Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. He stated the material from the release had been recovered and placed in drums onsite. He stated the release took place in the off-loading area of the pad. He stated he was notified of the released at 2345 hours (06/02).On 06/04/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection. I arrived at 0915 hours and met with Mr. Babcock. Environmental Resources was onsite to collect samples from the release and the prior release (CTS#396090). The area of the release was ~33 feet long (photo #2). There were no pooled fluids in the area of the release. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 452-1042 us/cm. The cause of the release was due to a valve malfunction (photo #3). Environmental resources screened the soil in the area of the release and received readings of 1-1.3 mS/cm (1000-1300 us/cm). The recovered material was observed in drums onsite and held within secondary containment (photo #4).The DEP screened the area of the prior release (CTS #396090). Fluids within the stormwater ditch at the release point were field measured for EC at ~452 us/cm. Mr. Babcock stated that this week there would be more material removed from the stormwater ditch at the release point due to elevated soil readings. There was dead vegetation observed downgrade of the affected bio-retention basin (photo #15-16). Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm. The violations related to the recent spill (CTS #398207) are considered immediately corrected however, outstanding violations remain open for API#015-23994 from the previous release (CTS #396090).I departed at 1120 hours.

In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EXPAND OPER LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/22/2026
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 8280314
Permit API: 015-23700
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/02/2026
Comments: Weather was 91¿¿ and sunny. There were no Expand representatives on location at time of inspection. Well appeared to be capable of production. Well had digital pressure monitoring equipment attached reading 916 PSI on the well head and 499 on the production tubing. Well had 3 annulus vents plumbed to surface with digital pressure monitoring equipment attached. A 48 hour pressure build up test was being conducted on the annulus vents. The 20" X 13 3/8" annulus vent read 16.01 PSI and 100% LEL and 58% methane was detected. The 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent read 0.00 PSI and 100% LEL and 4% methane was detected. The 9 5/8" X 5 1/2" annulus vent read 271.3 PSI and 100% LEL and 100% methane was detected. Creston took samples from the 20" X 13 3/8" and 9 5/8" X 5 1/2" annulus vents. Production and MIA reporting are in compliance with DEP regulations.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to ARMAC RESOURCES LLC in Warren City, Warren County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/05/2023 to ARMAC RESOURCES LLC in Warren City, Warren county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/05/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 993740
Permit API: 123-46905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/05/2023
Comments: On 05/05/2023, I responded to an email from my supervisor. Justin Hansen of Bull Run Resources called about a oil spill at the Warren railcar lease. The lease is owned and operated by Armac resources. It is located in the parking lot of Kope services in the town of Warren. Upon arrival a vac truck was on site recovering oil from the parking lot. Peat absorbent was being spread and raked around to soak up what couldn't be picked up with a vac truck.A mini excavator arrived and the crew started digging the gathering lines. A split in the line was found and repairs are being made. Soil impact in the trench was minimal. The crude came to the surface and ran approx 125 feet across the gravel lot. The crew is going to scrape the impacted gravel from the lot, along with any impacted soil from the trench, as well as oil soaked peat absorbent and oil absorbent pads used in the clean up. Justin informed me it will all be hauled to the McKean county land fill. An estimated 1-2 barrels of crude escaped.
